faq.a: Children's rights are the special rights every person under 18 has, set out in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child of 1989. They include the rights to survive, be protected, grow and be heard.

faq.q: What does the right to survive mean?
faq.a: It means every child has a right to life and to what they need to stay alive and healthy: food, clean water, health care and a home.
asks: Do children have a right to health care?

faq.q: What does the right to be protected mean?
faq.a: It means children must be kept safe from violence, abuse, neglect, dangerous work and exploitation, and cared for if they have no family to look after them.
asks: Tell me about to be protected

faq.q: Do children have a right to play?
faq.a: Yes. Article 31 of the Convention says every child has the right to rest, leisure, play and to join in cultural and artistic life. Along with education, play helps children grow.

faq.q: Do children have a right to be heard?
faq.a: Yes. Article 12 says children have the right to give their views on matters that affect them, and adults should take those views seriously, depending on the child's age and maturity.
asks: Tell me about to be heard

facts: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted on 20 November 1989; that date is now World Children's Day.
It has been ratified by 196 countries, every UN member except the United States, which has signed but not ratified it.

quiz.say: Which of these is a right in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
quiz.why: Article 31 gives every child the right to rest, leisure and play.

wrong.0: A phone is a want, not a right.
wrong.2: Rest and sleep are part of being healthy; staying up is not a right.

quiz.say: What does the right to be heard mean?
quiz.show: The right to be heard means…

options.show: Children can say what they think on things that affect them
options.say: Children can say what they think on things that affect them

quiz.why: Children's views should be listened to and taken seriously by adults making decisions.

wrong.0: Adults still decide, but must listen to children.
wrong.2: That is the opposite of the right to be heard.
